events.type: management commentary (supply and demand), CEO trip to Taiwan
events.summary: CEO Lisa Su spoke to reporters in Taipei on 2026-10-06 (Taiwan time, before the US open). Quotes as reported: 'We're going to substantially increase our supply in 2027'; 'There's very, very high demand for the next several years'; 'We have increased our own supply and capacity this year, but demand exceeds supply'; 'We used to plan capacity looking one to two years ahead. Now we are looking three to five years out.' She met TSMC, Hon Hai (Foxconn), Quanta, Acer and Asustek, and coverage says she plans to visit South Korea for memory talks. The Taipei Times names only the US$10 billion commitment AMD made in May 2026; no new investment figure was disclosed. Several outlets credit Reuters with first reporting the comments. AMD was up about 1.5% before the open as the news spread (Stocktwits).
events.why_it_matters: It is AMD's own CEO saying that supply, not demand, is what limits sales of its AI chips and server CPUs, and that supply will rise 'substantially' in 2027. That supports Pillar 1 (data-center growth) and Pillar 3 (deals delivered). It is also partly a rehash: in May 2026 Reuters reported AMD planned 'significantly more supply' for 2027 and beyond and a $10bn+ Taiwan investment. The new parts are the 3-to-5-year planning horizon and the fresh confirmation that demand still exceeds supply. The flip side: AMD cannot sell more than its partners (TSMC, memory makers) can build.

events.summary: Citi analyst Atif Malik kept a Buy rating and raised his AMD price target to $800 from $575. His reason: after Meta's 'Muse' AI agent launched, Citi raised its forecast for the CPU market from $29 billion in 2025 to $300 billion in 2030 (about 60% a year), and he expects AMD to be 'the primary beneficiary of the CPU renaissance', with Intel second. On the same day Mizuho (Vijay Rakesh) reportedly raised its target to $705 from $580 (Buy). This adds to Stifel's raise to $700 on 2026-10-05, which is already in the news log.
events.why_it_matters: This is an opinion, but it contains a model change (a much bigger CPU market forecast). It widens the AI case for AMD from GPUs to its EPYC server CPUs. Coverage of Tuesday's move names it as a driver. Price targets are opinions, not facts about value.

why_chain.text: Why they move the price: both say demand for AMD's chips is larger than it can currently supply and will stay high for years. More supply in 2027 means more revenue AMD can actually book, and Citi's model adds a second AI engine (server CPUs for AI agents) on top of GPUs.

Basic driver: investors' expectations of future AI computing spending, now including CPUs for 'agentic AI' since Meta's Muse launch (2026-09-21, already logged). Analysts' average EPS forecast roughly doubles from $7.59 (2026) to $15.72 (2027). Caveat: the 2027 supply message repeats what AMD said in May 2026, so part of the reaction is to a familiar story told again by the CEO in person.

products.name: AMD EPYC server CPUs (current generation; next generation 'Venice', Zen 6)
products.what_it_is: The main general-purpose processor in a data-center server: it runs the operating system and ordinary software, and in AI servers it feeds the GPUs.
products.analogy: If a GPU is a stadium full of calculators all doing one huge sum, the CPU is the manager who reads the instructions, hands out the work and does all the varied small jobs in between. AI agents create many more of those small jobs.
products.buyers: Cloud companies (Microsoft expanded its EPYC and Instinct partnership on 2026-07-20, per the AMD press-release list), enterprises and AI labs. Coverage says Meta's Muse agent runs on EPYC (Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-07, tier 3, not verified with AMD or Meta).
products.how_it_works: AI 'agents' (software that takes actions for a user: browsing, calling tools, running code) do many ordinary computing steps, not only GPU maths. Each step needs CPU time, so agents raise demand for server CPUs.
products.price: not available in this research (per-chip prices not gathered; AMD does not disclose average selling prices)
products.sales: Not disclosed separately. Labelled proxy: Data Center segment revenue $6.7bn in Q2 2026 (+107% y/y), which combines EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs. Market-share claims of about 46% appear in tier-3 articles without a named primary source (not verified).
products.stage: Current EPYC shipping in volume. 'Venice' (Zen 6) is the CPU in Helios racks (Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-10-07: 18 Venice CPUs per rack). Exact Venice shipment status not verified with AMD.
products.size_for_company: Part of Data Center, which was 58% of Q2 2026 revenue ($6.7bn of $11.5bn). CPU-only share: not disclosed.
products.competition: Intel Xeon; Arm-based chips designed by cloud companies; NVIDIA's own CPUs (coverage says NVIDIA is developing agent-focused CPUs; Yahoo Finance 2026-10-07, tier 3).
products.why_investors_care: Citi's forecast of the CPU market growing from $29bn (2025) to $300bn (2030) is an analyst estimate, not a fact. If even part of it happens, server CPUs become a second AI growth engine for AMD alongside GPUs. That is why Tuesday's target raise mattered.
products.watch_next: Server-CPU growth comments on the Q3 call (2026-11-03); Lisa Su's OCP keynote (2026-10-12); any CPU supply limits she flags.

products.name: AMD Helios rack with Instinct MI450-series (MI455X) GPUs
products.what_it_is: A complete AI server rack sold as one AI computer: 72 Instinct MI455X GPUs plus 18 EPYC 'Venice' CPUs, with networking and software (component counts per Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-10-07).
products.analogy: Instead of selling engines, AMD sells the whole car, ready to drive.
products.buyers: Helios customers named in coverage of Su's Taipei trip: OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle (Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-10-07; matches AMD's Q2 release list in the 2026-10-04 research). Anthropic makes Claude, which wrote this research.
products.how_it_works: Many GPUs are linked so they work as one large accelerator for training and running AI models. Customers commit to capacity measured in gigawatts of power.
products.sales: Not disclosed separately. Commitments: OpenAI 6 GW (2025 agreement); Anthropic up to 2 GW, first gigawatt from H1 2027. Labelled proxy: Data Center revenue $6.7bn in Q2 2026.
products.stage: Ramping from 2H 2026 per AMD (Q2 release). No new timing statement found in the window. Su's comment that supply is the constraint means it depends on TSMC wafers, packaging and HBM memory supply.
products.size_for_company: Data Center was 58% of Q2 2026 revenue; Helios share not disclosed.
products.competition: NVIDIA rack-scale systems (Vera Rubin); cloud companies' custom chips.
products.why_investors_care: Helios volume in late 2026 and 2027 is what 'substantially increase supply in 2027' would mostly feed.
products.watch_next: OCP keynote 2026-10-12; Q3 call 2026-11-03 for first Helios revenue and shipment timing; outcome of Su's memory talks in South Korea.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Supply, not demand, limits AMD: Su says demand exceeds supply even after 2026 increases, and memory (HBM) is tight across the industry; AMD depends on TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix for capacity.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Real near-term constraint (CEO's own words). It caps how much of the demand AMD can book in 2026 and makes 2027 growth depend on partners delivering. Medium concern; watch the Q3 call for supply comments.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Valuation is stretched: analysts' average targets ($619.51 to $662.38 across aggregators) are at or below the price; the stock trades at about 57x forward earnings vs a 5-year average of about 34x (Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-07, tier 3); RSI 72.2 and 71% above its 200-day average (metrics). Seeking Alpha contributors downgraded in September ('Too Hot To Touch', 'Likely Dead Money').
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Consistent with pipeline data; expectations are high going into 2026-11-03, the setup in which AMD fell 7% after a beat in August. Opinion pieces are low weight; the price data is solid.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Tuesday's 'news' is partly a rehash: in May 2026 Reuters reported AMD would have 'significantly more supply' for 2027 and beyond and announced a $10bn+ Taiwan investment.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Correct per the May coverage (the May details come from a search summary; the article was not opened). The new elements are the 3-to-5-year planning horizon and the in-person confirmation. That lowers the information value of the Taipei comments.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Rising rates hurt high-valuation chip stocks: on 2026-10-07 the 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.3% and chip stocks fell (SMH -1.18%).
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Single tier-3 source for the cause; the price data is solid. AMD's beta of about 3.2 makes it sensitive to rate moves. Macro risk, not company-specific.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Competition in CPUs for AI agents: NVIDIA is developing agent-focused CPUs, cloud companies build their own chips, and Intel is also named as a beneficiary.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Plausible and ongoing; Intel fell 2% on Tuesday while AMD rose (24/7 Wall St.), suggesting investors currently favour AMD. Low-medium concern.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Product delays: Zen 6 desktop CPUs reportedly slipped to 2027; MI455X/Helios delay rumours in February 2026.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: The desktop slip is leak-based and affects PCs, not the AI thesis. The Helios rumours were denied by AMD (Windows Report, NextPlatform). Not a trigger; check Helios timing at OCP on 2026-10-12 and on the Q3 call.
